speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; to begin, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is this pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic presentation of sciatica. Did the pain start immediately during a specific movement or lift, or did it begin spontaneously? Also, do you notice any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your leg or foot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation (Sciatica). 

The clinical picture of sudden, sharp lower back pain radiating to the foot during exercise, accompanied by worsening pain with movement, is highly characteristic of a herniated disc compressing the sciatic nerve. This diagnosis is supported by your history and current symptoms without requiring further imaging at this stage.
